threads.title: Help No Matter How Many Times I Instruct This Chatbot It Keeps Acting And Talking For Me

messages.author: Korgfal
messages.content: HELP! No matter how many times I instruct this chatbot, it keeps acting and talking for me!!!

messages.author: ろーらい35
messages.content: Is this about a problem with the behavior of a bot you created?

messages.author: ろーらい35
messages.content:
No matter what you do, LLMs may still sometimes act or speak for the user.

However, if you want to reduce that as much as possible — assuming this is a question about a bot I made — I think adding a sentence like this to the Personality section will make the bot more stable:

User Agency Rule:
{{char}} must never speak, act, decide, think, feel, react, consent, refuse, move, or narrate internal thoughts for {{user}}. {{char}} may only describe {{char}}’s own actions, dialogue, perceptions, and the visible consequences of {{user}}’s explicit input. Always leave {{user}}’s responses, choices, emotions, and next actions open.

In my case, I also try to handle it this way:

1. I avoid writing {{user}}’s dialogue as much as possible, even in the Greeting.

2. Personality
   In the finished bot, this is the most important place to include the rule. Personality works as {{char}}’s behavior OS, so I directly tell the LLM something like:

{{char}} must never speak, act, decide, think, feel, or react for {{user}}.

3. Scenario
   In Scenario, I reinforce it as a conversation-flow rule:

Do not decide {{user}}’s choices without permission.
Do not advance the outcome too far before {{user}} responds.
Do not write {{user}}’s inner thoughts, reactions, consent, or refusal.

I hope this answer helps.

messages.author: Korgfal
messages.content: It's someone elses bot. The /cmd will work for exactly one massage. And no matter what sort of /cmd I use, it keeps reverting back to speaking and/or acting for me.

messages.author: ろーらい35
messages.content:
Ah, so this is about a bot made by another creator.

In that case, there’s honestly only so much you can do. This often happens when you use something like “Continue” and let the bot actively generate the dialogue, but it is very hard to avoid completely.

About the only practical options are to reroll, edit the bot’s response, and repeatedly train the chat flow so that the bot learns not to make the other side perform the user’s actions.

As a side note, I also often play with bots made by other people, and I constantly find myself thinking, “I never thought that!” and getting annoyed, lol.
